findings.title: The substituted period-wall sentence hardcodes "now closed" and "have that year reopened", but the wall it replaces also fires for a fiscal year in `closing`
findings.spec_line: #987 Desired behavior: "When this refusal surfaces anywhere in the opening-basis flow, the words presented describe it in terms of the opening basis being worked on (for example, that the basis is dated into a closed year), not a raw journal-entry id the person never created. The underlying rule, refusal code, and firing point (draft, never approval) do not change." Out of scope: "Changing which fiscal-year boundary is enforced or when the wall fires."
findings.evidence: apps/web/messages/en.json:4181 `OpeningCarryDown.seed.closedPeriodRefusal` = "This opening basis is dated into a fiscal year that is now closed, so it cannot be changed here. Date it into an open fiscal year, or have that year reopened, before trying again." It is substituted for EVERY CLR19/write_into_closed_period refusal on the workbench (opening-seed-workbench.tsx:117-131). But `clara._tf_period_wall_lines` (0056_wave_e_close_model.sql:735) returns early only when `v_fy.status in ('open','reopened')`, and `clara.fiscal_years.status` is checked `in ('open','closing','closed','reopened')` (0056:241-242). So the wall fires for a `closing` year too - a real, reachable state set by begin-close (`update clara.fiscal_years set status = 'closing'`, 0056:1770 and 0120_f_a4_pr_1b_close_lifecycle.sql:1124), and the wall's own FY lookup deliberately PREFERS it (`order by (fy.status in ('closing','closed')) desc`, 0056:733). The generic message it replaces was status-accurate: `raise exception 'entry % sits in % fiscal year %'` (0056:746) interpolates `v_fy.status`. The substitution therefore tells a person mid-close that the year is "closed" and points them at "have that year reopened" - reopen applies to a CLOSED year, not one still inside a close run, so the remedy sentence names the wrong door. The information needed to get this right is already on the wire: the refusal detail carries `fy_status` (0056:748-749) and `RefusalError.detail` exposes the whole typed detail object (apps/web/lib/wire.ts:123-127). Both #987 cells mock `fy_status: "closed"` only (opening-refusal-and-staleness.test.tsx:296 and the L07-05 cell at :351), so nothing covers `closing`.
findings.required_fix: Branch the substituted sentence on `error.detail?.fy_status`: keep today's wording for `closed`, and add a `closing` variant that says the year is being closed and names the close run as what must finish or be abandoned (never "reopened"). Add a cell that drives the same CLR19 refusal with `fy_status: "closing"`. If the owner would rather keep one sentence, it must be status-neutral (e.g. "a fiscal year that is no longer open") and must not name reopen as the only way back.

findings.title: The tick refreshes only the task rows, so a completed extraction leaves the panel's extraction badge, Facts view and state panel stale - and no Refresh is offered in that state
findings.spec_line: #904 Desired behavior: "While any task is `queued`, `held_egress` or `running`, THE PANEL re-reads on the same cadence and trigger style one of the existing idioms uses (the workbench settle poll, or the client-home 30 s plus visible-return pattern), and stops once every task is terminal." Current behavior: "A task that moves from `running` to `done` or `failed` while the panel is open is not reflected until a reload."
findings.evidence: After the L07-02 fix round, `onTick` is `listProcessingTasksForDocument(documentId)` alone and its result is held in a local `taskOverride` (document-detail.tsx:139-147). Only `DocumentMetadata`'s task list consumes it (document-detail.tsx:253 `tasks={tasks}`); `data.document`, `data.extractions` and `data.regions` are never re-read. So when the last task flips to `done` the poll stops (`enabled` goes false) and the panel is left self-contradictory: the tasks strip says "Extraction complete" while the extraction badge above it still renders the mount-time `doc.extraction_status` (`documentBadges(doc)`, document-metadata.tsx:98-100, fed by lib/documents/copy.ts:139) and the Facts view still renders the mount-time `data.regions` (document-detail.tsx:245, :294). The manual Refresh the fix round added is gated on `tasksExhausted = tasksPoll.exhausted && a task is still non-terminal` (document-detail.tsx:257) - exactly the OPPOSITE case - so in the settled case the person has no affordance at all and must reload the browser, which is the defect the ticket opened on. The sibling idiom the lane cites does exactly what is missing here: the receipts poll re-reads narrowly per tick and then pays the FULL derivation once, on the settling tick (documents-workbench.tsx:77-97, `narrowRef.current = false; // settled: pay the other three reads once, then stop`), and apps/web/README.md's own rewritten paragraph quotes that law ("the full mount sequence is paid again exactly once, on the tick where the batch settles") for receipts while describing no equivalent for this poll. document-detail-live-refresh.test.tsx:238 pins the gap in the other direction: "a tick must not re-read extractions" - with no cell for the settling tick.
findings.required_fix: On the tick where the last non-terminal task becomes terminal, run one full `reload()` (the receipts poll's own settled-tick law), keeping the narrow one-read cost for every intermediate tick. Add a cell asserting that after the running-to-done transition the bundle reads (`documents`, `document_extractions`, `document_regions`) grow exactly once. Alternatively - if the owner prefers to keep the one-read ceiling absolutely - render the Refresh affordance whenever the override reports a status different from the bundle's, so the stale badge and Facts are at least recoverable in one click.

findings.title: `watermark` is left as the exact half-state the brief forbids: typed on the envelope, read by nothing
findings.spec_line: #903 Desired behavior: "`watermark` is removed from the review-queue envelope type (and from the needs-you type if nothing else carries it), UNLESS the implementer finds a real consumer, in which case it is threaded through the hook to that consumer; NO HALF-STATE WHERE IT IS TYPED BUT DROPPED." AC2: "`watermark` is either fully wired to a renderer or fully absent from the types; a grep proves no dangling reference."
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/firm/needs-you.ts:243-254 now declares `watermark?: unknown` with a comment that states outright it is "NOT rendered by this build". The lane's own new cell pins that non-read: use-review-queue.test.ts:98-104 asserts `assert.doesNotMatch(hookSource, /\.watermark\b/)`. No consumer was found or wired, so neither of the brief's two permitted outcomes was reached. The recheck already flagged this as RC-01 and it is still open at HEAD 278f0795. Two further points the recheck did not make: (a) the field's type was also WEAKENED in the process - `main` had `watermark: string` (required, string-typed), HEAD has `watermark?: unknown`, so the diff is a net loss of type information on a field the DB really does emit as a value (`clara.list_review_queue`, 0011_daily_loop.sql:3861, recut 0016_a21_compliance_watch.sql:4691); (b) the file's `compliance`/`lint` precedent the comment leans on predates this ticket and was never put to the owner as an answer to AC2, so it cannot silently override the brief.
findings.required_fix: Pick one of the brief's two forks and say so against AC2. Either (i) restore `watermark: string`, thread it through `use-review-queue.ts` and render it - noting that #903's own out-of-scope line reads "A new freshness indicator for the review queue", which argues against this fork - or (ii) delete it from the type again and record the CONTEXT.md/estate-concept honesty gap in prose (apps/web/README.md or a comment at the deletion site) so the L07-A03 complaint about a false justification is answered without re-creating the forbidden half-state. If the owner rules the `compliance`/`lint` posture acceptable, that ruling belongs in a comment on #903, not implicit in the diff.

findings.title: The substitution also drops the fiscal-year LABEL, which the ticket never asked to remove
findings.spec_line: #987 Current behavior: "...refused by the shared period-wall check, NAMING THE FISCAL-YEAR LABEL AND THE ID OF THE JOURNAL ENTRY it would have created". Desired behavior: "...not a raw journal-entry id the person never created."
findings.evidence: The ticket names two things the generic message carries and asks for exactly one of them to go. The new sentence (en.json:4181) names neither: it says "a fiscal year that is now closed" with no label, where the DB message said "sits in closed fiscal year FY2026" (0056_wave_e_close_model.sql:746, interpolating `v_fy.label`). A client with more than one closed or closing year now cannot tell from the refusal which year refused. The refusal `detail` carries `fiscal_year_id` but not the label (0056:748-749), so recovering it needs a lookup - which is why this is minor rather than major - but the loss is real and undeclared: neither wave1-lane07-final.md nor the code comment mentions that the label went with the entry id.
findings.required_fix: Either surface the year (interpolate a label resolved from `fiscal_year_id` against the workbench's own fiscal-year read, or carry it from the refusal message the way other lanes read door text), or record explicitly in the report and the code comment that #987 was read as dropping the label too, so the owner can rule on it.

findings.title: Eight typed test fixtures still have `watermark` stripped - dead residue of the reverted deletion, now making the fixtures less faithful to the wire

The typed fixtures now do the opposite of their untyped siblings, for no reason left in the diff.
findings.required_fix: Restore `watermark` to the eight typed fixtures (matching the untyped mock bodies and the real wire shape), or - if fork (ii) of CRS-07-03 is taken and the field is deleted again - leave them stripped and say so. Either way the diff should not carry the half-applied remains of a reverted decision.

findings.title: apps/web/README.md's #876 paragraph miscounts the mount calls and calls the new projection "narrower" when it is nine times wider
findings.spec_line: #876 Desired behavior: "A read in the documents read module accepts a set of document ids and returns live filing state for exactly those... The intake-receipts load switches to it, scoped to its intake rows." Key interfaces: "The documents read module: a new document-set read beside the existing two, SAME PROJECTED COLUMNS."
findings.evidence: apps/web/README.md (the rewritten 'Three regions on the client tab' bullet) says "The mount pays THREE calls in two phases" and then enumerates four (intake view, unassigned set, caller_context, then the bounded filings read), referring to the last as "That fourth call" two sentences later. The same paragraph describes the tradeoff as "one extra serial round trip per mount for a narrower, ID-bounded projection". It is not narrower: the pre-#876 query was `document_filings?client_id=eq.<id>&retired_at=is.null&select=document_id` - ONE column (receipts.ts, deleted hunk) - while `listActiveFilingsForDocuments` selects `FILING_COLS`, nine columns (reads.ts:36, 63-70). The read is narrower in ROWS and wider in COLUMNS. The column widening itself is correct - the brief explicitly asks for "same projected columns" - so this is a documentation defect, not an implementation one, but it is the paragraph a future lane will measure the over-read claim against.
findings.required_fix: Correct the paragraph: say FOUR calls in two phases, and state the tradeoff honestly - one extra serial round trip and a nine-column projection, in exchange for a result bounded to the intake rows' own document ids instead of the client's entire active-filing set.

findings.title: AC1's "error behaviour" leg is not delivered, and the stated reason is not quite right
findings.spec_line: #900 AC1: "The answer input renders through `Field` with the same label, HELP AND ERROR BEHAVIOUR the sibling surfaces show." Desired behavior: "Each field-shaped part is composed with `Field` / `FieldGroup` consistent with the sibling surfaces (label, help text, ERROR PLACEMENT, spacing)."
findings.evidence: InterviewRunCard.tsx:290-322 composes `FieldGroup`/`Field`/`FieldLabel`/`FieldDescription` but no `FieldError`. wave1-lane07-final.md justifies this as "`submitAnswer` has no field-scoped refusal shape today (every failure becomes the card's existing `run.error` banner - chrome, out of scope here)". The first half is true, the second half understates it: a failed answer submit IS this field's own failure, and it renders at InterviewRunCard.tsx:307 (`{run.error ? <StateBanner tone="error">...` inside `CardContent`), which sits ABOVE the thread log and the attachment slot - far from the textarea the person must correct. The sibling surfaces the ticket points at place the message beside the control (trade-invoice-form.tsx:575-701, invite-dialog.tsx:132, matching-candidates.tsx:211). The owner's 2026-09-18 ruling scopes the CHROME out, which is a fair reading of "the card's chrome... stays", but the ruling does not say the error leg of AC1 is waived, and neither the report nor the code comment says AC1 was delivered two-thirds.
findings.required_fix: Either render `run.error` through a `FieldError` inside the answer `Field` when the failure came from `submitAnswer` (leaving start and cancel failures in the chrome banner), or state against AC1 explicitly that the error leg is deferred because no field-scoped refusal exists, and say where the failure does surface. A one-line note in the code comment beside the `Field` would do.

findings.title: `CENTS_PARTICULARS` covers five basis keys against the ticket's explicit out-of-scope line for "any other basis particular"
findings.spec_line: #842 Out of scope: "Any other basis particular (NONE IS CENTS-TYPED TODAY)." Summary: "Render a stated `settled_cents` as money in the periodic-adjustment history disclosure."
findings.evidence: periodic-adjustments-table.tsx:150-162 defines `CENTS_PARTICULARS` as five keys - `amount_cents`, `opening_cents`, `closing_cents`, `adjustment_cents`, `settled_cents` - and the fix round added `842.amount` and `842.stock` cells for the four the ticket excluded. The triage premise the out-of-scope line rests on is demonstrably false: `clara._adjustment_basis_canonical` (0212_payroll_settled_cents.sql:290-332) builds all five through `clara._adjustment_cents_value`, which returns `bigint` (0194_periodic_adjustments.sql:470-475). So the widening is technically correct and closes a real, identical defect. It is still a deliberate override of a line the ticket wrote, made by the lane rather than the owner, and neither the report nor the code comment frames it that way - the code comment presents the five-key set as if the ticket had asked for it.
findings.required_fix: No code change needed. Name it as an override in the report and on #842, quoting the out-of-scope line and the migration evidence that retires it, so the ticket is not closed against a criterion it no longer matches. If the owner would rather keep #842 literal, split the four extra keys into their own ticket and revert `CENTS_PARTICULARS` to `settled_cents` plus the two new cells.

findings.title: AC1's cell proves what the dialog's SOURCE says, not what it renders - a literal option would slip past it
findings.spec_line: #878 AC1: "A CELL PROVES THE DETAIL DIALOG NO LONGER OFFERS `consent_evidence` (or renders the inline explanation before an avoidable refusal)."
findings.evidence: document-kind-labels.test.tsx:180-208 reads document-kind-dialog.tsx as text and asserts three regexes: that it imports `CLASSIFIABLE_DOCUMENT_KINDS`, that it calls `CLASSIFIABLE_DOCUMENT_KINDS.map(`, and that it does not call `DOCUMENT_KINDS.map(`. It never mounts the dialog. A hand-written `<SelectItem value="consent_evidence">` added beside the map, or an options list built with `.flatMap`/spread instead of `.map`, would leave all three assertions green while the defect returned. The lane's justification (base-ui's Select popup mounts lazily, and the [633] fix-round cell set the source-pin precedent) is accurate and the risk is low, but the cell is a proxy for AC1, not AC1.
findings.required_fix: Strengthen with one assertion that does not need the popup open - e.g. `assert.doesNotMatch(dialogSource, /consent_evidence/)`, proving the string appears nowhere in the file at all - or render the dialog and assert no `SelectItem`-shaped node carries that value. Alternatively record in the report and on the ticket that AC1 is met by source pin under the [633] idiom.

summary: Nine SPEC findings across seven of the lane's eight tickets (#896 is clean). Three are major: (1) #987's substituted refusal hardcodes 'now closed' and 'have that year reopened', but the period wall it replaces also fires for a fiscal year in `closing` (0056:735 returns early only for open/reopened; 0056:241 admits `closing`), so the sentence misstates the state and names the wrong remedy for a client mid-close - and `fy_status` is already on the refusal detail, so the distinction was available; (2) #904's tick was narrowed to the task rows alone, so when the last task settles the panel is left showing 'Extraction complete' beside a mount-time extraction badge and a mount-time Facts view, with no Refresh offered (that renders only on `exhausted`) - the sibling receipts poll the lane cites pays the full derivation exactly once on the settling tick and this one does not; (3) #903 leaves `watermark` as `watermark?: unknown`, typed and read by nothing, which is verbatim the 'half-state where it is typed but dropped' the brief forbids, and also weakens the field from the required `string` main carried. Six minors: #987 also silently drops the fiscal-year label the ticket never asked to lose; #903's eight typed fixtures still carry the stripped-out `watermark` from the reverted deletion; apps/web/README.md's #876 paragraph miscounts the mount calls and calls a nine-column projection 'narrower' than the one-column query it replaced; #900 delivers label and help but not AC1's error leg, on a reason that does not quite hold; #842 widens `CENTS_PARTICULARS` to five keys against an explicit out-of-scope line (correctly, on migration evidence, but as an undeclared override); #878's AC1 is met by a source-text pin rather than rendered behaviour. Every cell the lane cites was re-run green at HEAD (92 tests across 12 files), and the lane's 'none already satisfied, none stopped' determination is independently confirmed against the merge-base.
